extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH R21 (PA-10-069) / NIAID exploratory developmental research grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a PHS 398 / SF424 R&R-format R21 grant application to NIH/NIAID, including required forms, budget, biosketches, human/animal approvals, and resource-sharing statements. Emphasis on meeting FOA and NIH formatting, content, and compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format. Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific FOA (PA-10-069 / parent R21) instructions and any updated NIH/NIAID guidance rather than relying solely on sample applications; check for updated forms, page limits, and policies before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and assurances / signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing this application, I certify (1) to the statements contained in the list of certifications* and (2) that the statements herein are true, complete and accurate to the best of my knowledge. I also provide the required assurances * and agree to comply with any resulting terms if I accept an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized institutional official must sign; false statements may carry criminal/civil penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). Ensure required certifications and assurances are included or linked as required by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF 424 (R&R) face page fields
rubrics_metrics.description: SF 424 R&R Face Page required fields: Type of Submission, Federal Identifier, Applicant Organizational DUNS, Legal Name, Department, Street, City, State, ZIP, Country, Person to be contacted (name, phone, fax, email), Employer Identification (EIN/TIN), Type of Applicant, Proposed Project Start/End Dates, Descriptive Title of Applicant's Project, Type of Application (New/Resubmission/Renewal/Continuation/Revision), Congressional District, and other standard face page data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete, accurate organizational and PD/PI contact information, DUNS, EIN, and ensure the application type and project dates align with FOA instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Specific Cover Page Supplement items
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement includes Human Subjects questions (Clinical Trial? Agency-defined Phase III?), Human Embryonic Stem Cell questions, and related PD/PI and applicant contact info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer human subjects, clinical trial, and HESC questions accurately; include IRB/assurance identifiers or exemption statements as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract (Description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary: a concise description of the proposed research (e.g., summary of Legionella GPS screen approach, aims, methods, and significance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, stand-alone abstract suitable for reviewers and public reporting; include key objectives, approach, and expected outcomes; adhere to FOA-specified length and content limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance Statement (Project Narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Narrative: a separate statement describing the public health relevance of the proposed research (e.g., potential to identify targets for new antibiotics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how the work addresses public health needs; keep it non-technical and within any specified length limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe available laboratory and institutional resources: lab square footage, tissue culture rooms, laminar flow hoods, CO2 incubators, microscopes, equipment (centrifuges, FACS, thermal cyclers, -80C freezers, liquid N2), computing resources, library access, animal facility access, and administrative/statistical/bioinformatics support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the environment and resources are adequate to accomplish the aims; list shared and dedicated equipment, collaborators and consultation arrangements, and space allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and intellectual environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the scientific interactions and institutional environment that will support the project (e.g., departmental seminars, collaborations with named faculty, consultation plans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the institutional environment, collaborators, and planned interactions will enhance project success; name key consultations and frequency if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims: a succinct list of the study's aims (appears in PHS 398 Research Plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State one-page (or FOA-specified) Specific Aims clearly and realistically; each aim should be testable and linked to the overall objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan: Research Strategy (Significance, Innovation, Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy should include background, significance, innovation, and an approach detailing experiments, methodologies, anticipated results, alternatives, and contingency plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address rigor and reproducibility, potential pitfalls and alternatives, and how results will be interpreted; ensure methods match aims and the project is feasible within the proposed budget and period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan: ORFeome/gain-of-function and GPS screening methodology (example content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: In this application, detailed methodological description of GPS screening, creation of GPS reporter cell lines, gain-of-function screens of ~150 Dot/Icm effectors, use of tetracycline-regulated expression systems, flow cytometry readouts, and downstream genetic validation in L. pneumophila.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient methodological detail for reviewers to assess feasibility and rigor; justify chosen assays and controls and discuss how redundancy and cytotoxicity concerns will be managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Include literature cited relevant to the proposal (e.g., supporting publications for GPS platform and Legionella biology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite key prior work to justify rationale and methodology; adhere to citation formatting and any page constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach letters indicating institutional or collaborator support (e.g., access to libraries, reagents, expertise; a lab head's letter offering access to GPS libraries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide succinct, specific letters that confirm resource/access commitments and clarify the nature of contributions (e.g., provision of effector ORFs, equipment access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketches for Senior/Key Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide biographical sketches for each listed Senior/Key Person. 'DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.' Include Personal Statement, Positions and Honors, Education/Training, Selected peer-reviewed publications, and Research Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PHS 398 biosketch format and page limit; include relevant publications and current & pending support; tailor personal statement to the project role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile details and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Senior/Key Person Profile entries: name, project role, contact information, project role category, attach biographical sketch and Current & Pending Support documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accuracy of roles and availability; attach required supporting documents for each key person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: PHS 398 Modular Budget and required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Modular Budget information for each budget period: Direct Costs, Indirect Costs (Indirect Cost Type and Rate), Consortium F&A, Total Direct and Indirect Costs, Cognizant Agency contact, Indirect Cost Rate Agreement Date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide modular budgets consistent with FOA limits; include accurate indirect cost rates and cognizant agency details; attach budget justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justifications (Personnel, Consortium, Narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget Justifications must be provided (Personnel Justification, Consortium Justification, Additional Narrative Justification) explaining personnel effort and consortium arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify requested personnel and consortium costs with roles, percent effort, and responsibilities; include narrative rationale for equipment, supplies, and other direct costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protections and IRB information
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer: Are Human Subjects Involved? IRB Approval Date; Human Subject Assurance Number; Is the Project Exempt? If YES to Human Subjects, provide details/explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide IRB approval or exemption details as applicable; include plans for protection of human subjects, consent, and data confidentiality according to NIH policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals protections and IACUC information
rubrics_metrics.description: Answer: Are Vertebrate Animals Used? IACUC Approval Date; Animal Welfare Assurance Number; provide explanations if yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide IACUC approval or assurance numbers and compliance with animal welfare regulations; describe animal use and humane care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research and biosafety compliance statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether select agents will be used. Example text: 'No select agents will be used in this project. The BL-2 work proposed in this application have been approved by Harvard’s Committee on Microbiological Safety. All safety procedures for use with BL-2 level pathogens will be followed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If select agents are involved, include required registration numbers and compliance statements; describe biosafety level and institutional approvals for pathogen work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact / NEPA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If this project has an actual or potential impact on the environment, indicate whether an exemption has been authorized or an environmental assessment (EA) or environmental impact statement (EIS) has been performed and provide explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address any environmental compliance requirements and include supporting documentation if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign activities / international collaborations disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this project involve activities outside of the United States or partnerships with international collaborators? If yes, identify countries and provide optional explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose international components and justify foreign activities; ensure compliance with any FOA-specific restrictions regarding foreign components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance site and project/ performance site location information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Project/Performance Site(s) primary location information: organization name, street, city, county, state, ZIP, country, DUNS, and congressional district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List all performance sites and any additional locations; ensure consistency with organizational DUNS and institutional approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan (materials/data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research resources generated will be freely distributed upon request to qualified academic investigators for non-commercial research, adhering to NIH Grants Policy on Sharing of Unique Research Resources. Material transfers would be made with no more restrictive terms than the Simple Letter Agreement or the UBMTA. IP requiring a patent will be managed to ensure broad availability per NIH Principles and Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concrete plan for sharing reagents, constructs, and data, specify MTA terms (SLAs/UBMTA), and commit to NIH resource-sharing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Checklist and administrative questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the PHS 398 Checklist including Application Type, Change of Investigator/Institution questions, Inventions and Patents disclosure (renewal apps), Program Income, Disclosure Permission Statement, and other administrative items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer administrative checklist items accurately and provide required supporting documentation (e.g., program income details, disclosure permissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and formatting constraints (biosketches and other sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit page limits stated (e.g., 'BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH ... DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES' for each biosketch) and implicit requirements to follow FOA-specified formats and OMB form constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to page limits and formatting rules in the FOA and forms; noncompliant pages may be removed from review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current and pending support disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach Current & Pending Support for PD/PI and key personnel as required in Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose all sources of research support (active and pending) to allow assessment of overlap and effort; ensure accuracy and institutional approval.
